big: A fund's factsheet says 14% over three years. A client invested in it and her own return is 9%. Did the fund lie? No. Published returns assume one lump sum held for the full period, in one plan, before tax. Hers did not.

lines: Why does my return differ from the fund's?

Your return depends on when each rupee went in and came out. Two people in the same fund over the same three years can differ a lot. Add plan type, exit loads, taxes and switches. XIRR is the tool for personal returns.

rows: one lump sum, full period, before tax
SIPs and a withdrawal on different dates
regular plan, exit load, tax, switches
XIRR: counts timing and size of each cash flow

q: Published fund returns usually assume what?
opts: Returns shown after all taxes paid
Returns shown after exit loads paid
One lump sum held the full period
why: SIPs would need XIRR. It does not answer what was asked.
Published returns are before tax. The details here point elsewhere.
Exit loads are not counted. That does not match this case.
That is the standard assumption. That matches the case described.

q: Two people hold the same fund for three years with different entry dates. What follows?
opts: Their returns must be exactly equal
why: Equal returns need equal timing. That does not match this case.
Timing of each rupee changes the result. This fits the facts given.

q: Which tool captures the timing and size of each cash flow?
why: XIRR accounts for every dated cash flow.
Point-to-point assumes a single lump sum.
Dividend yield is a payout ratio.

q: Which of these can widen the gap between a published and a personal return?
opts: The font used on the factsheet page
The brand colour of the fund house
Plan type, exit loads, taxes, switches
The weather on the day of investing
why: A font does not matter. It does not fit the facts given.
A colour does not matter. It does not answer what was asked.
These all change what the investor actually keeps.
Weather does not matter. That does not match this case.

pts: Published returns assume one lump sum, one plan, before tax.
Personal returns depend on timing, plan, loads, tax and switches.
XIRR is the right tool for personal returns.
